rv.q: Within this gimmickry, Threlfall delivers a fairly classic Lear, deeply affecting in the deathbed scenes but, having established the character’s nationalism, winning a big laugh with the usually nothing line, “Am I in France ?”
This is a King Lear that is a truly gripping masterpiece.
For a city that prides itself on doing things differently, this is a brilliantly alternative take on the work.
Threlfall delivers the monarch in all his terrible, heartbreaking glory but this is a production that promises so much but never quite matches his stature.
Overall, King Lear is a powerful, thought-provoking night at the theatre, anchored by Threlfall's compelling performance and a story that proves some family problems really are timeless.

In a year of notable Lears – including Maureen Beattie’s superb, feminised monarch in Pitlochry and Ian McDiarmid’s memorable playing in Sheffield – the impressive David Threlfall is let down by a frustratingly uneven production at the Royal Exchange in Manchester.

cn.t: David Threlfall delivers a compelling, powerful Lear in this bold but uneven production. Critics praise his outstanding performance and dark humor, though Dunster's disruptive choices—including merging King and Fool—prove divisive.
